About this page

On this page

Batteries Included ​

Feluqa brings common application capabilities together so a team can focus on its Product's workflows. The direction is batteries included, but removable: capabilities should have clear contracts and be replaceable where an Application needs a different implementation.

Feluqa's ambition is to become the standard all-in-one ecosystem for building Rust applications: the breadth of reusable components associated with Symfony, the developer experience associated with Laravel, a product-building layer in the spirit of Filament, and first-class desktop experiences that belong alongside environments such as KDE. These are references for the coherence and reach Feluqa aims to offer, not claims of feature parity or affiliation.

The goal is a connected system of components, tools, and conventions that teams can adopt as a whole or compose around their needs. “All in one” does not mean every capability must be fused into one runtime: components should have clear boundaries and contracts.

Some foundations are already available. Other capabilities are incomplete or still product goals. The status beside each area describes Feluqa today; it does not promise that every battery is finished or replaceable yet.

Terms used on this page ​

TermMeaning here
Asynchronous (async)A way to express work that can pause while waiting and resume later, allowing a runtime to schedule other work in the meantime.
Asynchronous runtimeThe executor and supporting services that poll asynchronous tasks and provide facilities such as network I/O and timers.
TokioThe asynchronous runtime used by Feluqa's current server profile.
AxumThe HTTP web framework used by Feluqa's current server profile.
AdapterA boundary that connects a library or protocol to a framework, such as an Axum adapter for the Inertia server protocol.
Inertia.jsA way to build server-routed single-page applications with a frontend framework. The Rust inertia-omega project provides an alpha server implementation and Axum adapter; Feluqa has not selected it.
BatteryA capability Feluqa makes available or aims to provide through a documented contract. “Removable” is a product requirement; it does not mean every current capability can already be replaced.

The major capabilities ​

Application and runtime foundation ​

Application foundation

In progress

SDK, compile-time checks, and application metadata establish shared contracts. Application composition is still being completed.

Async execution

Server foundation

The server profile uses Tokio for asynchronous tasks, network I/O, and timers.

Web and APIs

Available; evolving

Axum handles HTTP routing with Tower services and middleware. Inertia support remains a possible future integration.

Platform and data services ​

Identity and access

Foundations available

Accounts, roles, server-side sessions, CSRF, tenant identities, and audit persistence are available. The complete System Panel is unfinished.

Data persistence

Available foundations

SQLite and PostgreSQL support uses SeaORM, named pools, and embedded migrations. Backup and restore need release qualification.

Panels and resources

Integration in progress

The panel catalogue and typed UI schemas provide shared contracts. The full System Panel and UI integration remain incomplete.

Live actions

Typed dispatch available

Signed, typed actions are supported. Browser reconciliation and shared replay protection remain unfinished.

Development, extension, and operations ​

Modules

Static composition

Applications compose statically compiled Rust modules. Dynamic installation, upgrades, and removal remain product goals.

Console and CLI

Available; evolving

The CLI and console framework provide project commands, named binaries, profiles, and handlers.

Deployment

Product target

Standalone builds, deployment, rollback, backup, and restore are not yet a qualified end-to-end path.

Agent workflows

Product direction

Agents should inspect, propose, validate, and package changes through explicit, reviewable steps. The complete workflow is not available yet.

Each area above is labelled with its current status. Feluqa's implementation continues to evolve, so the capability guides describe what is available and what remains a product direction.
